_comment: Manually-authored (manual-agent-pass-v1) agentic workflow spec for the AAMI claims-coverage process map, transcribed and elaborated from the debate-vetted worked example in docs/agentic-workflow-design.md §5/§9. Generated against process-map v2. See skills/agentic-workflow-synthesis/SKILL.md.

spec.goal: Produce a normalized intake bundle (claim record + attached files) from the first notice of loss channel.
spec.trigger: Policyholder submits a claim via app, phone transcript, or web form.

inputs.schema: raw FNOL payload: channel, free-text/transcript, attached files (photos, police report if provided)

spec.decision_logic: Pass-through / storage operation only. No interpretation.

grounding.reason: No claims cited — pure ingestion, no policy interpretation.

spec.error_handling: Malformed/unreadable attachment retried 3x, then flagged to claim record as 'attachment_unreadable' (does not block intake).
spec.audit: Full raw payload + attachment hashes logged.

nodes.title: Extract & normalize facts into a claim packet

spec.goal: Produce a structured claim packet (incident date/time/location, parties, vehicle, described damage) from the raw intake bundle.

outputs.schema: {claim_id, structured_fields: {incident_date, incident_location, parties[], vehicle_id, described_damage}, incident_narrative}

spec.decision_logic: Deterministic field extraction (structured form fields) + passthrough of the free-text narrative unmodified for downstream agent steps. No coverage interpretation happens here.

grounding.reason: Extraction/normalization only — the definition of 'incident' (incident_definition) governs what counts as one incident for BR-01/AG steps downstream, not this node's own logic.

spec.error_handling: Required structured field missing -> claim_packet.missing_facts[] populated, still passed downstream (BR-01/GW-01 handles escalation).
spec.audit: Structured fields + narrative logged verbatim alongside source attachment references.

nodes.title: Verify policyholder identity against certificate of insurance
nodes.source_task_title: Verify policyholder identity against certificate of insurance

spec.goal: Confirm the identity of the person submitting the claim matches the certificate of insurance on file.
spec.decision_logic: Exact/fuzzy-match lookup against the certificate of insurance record (name, policy number, DOB). Boolean outcome, no interpretation.

grounding.reason: Operational identity check, not a policy-coverage rule — no PDS clause governs it.

spec.error_handling: Lookup service unavailable -> retry 3x with backoff, then route to Data Correction queue (does not silently pass).
spec.audit: Match result + fields compared logged (not raw PII beyond what's already on the claim record).

spec.goal: Decide whether the claim is eligible to proceed to coverage analysis.

inputs.schema: {policy_version_id, effective_dates, incident_date, territory, insured_item, endorsement_set, mandatory_fact_presence_flags}

spec.decision_logic: Hard rules only, no inference: incident date outside policy period -> fail. Required fields absent or source documents conflict -> needs_human. No discretion beyond the coded rule table.

grounding.fabrication_check: every reason_code maps to a real clause/page from the pinned policy version
grounding.misapplication_check: not applicable to pure rule evaluation — rules are pre-verified against source at authoring time, not re-verified per claim

confidence_escalation_trigger.reason: deterministic node — no confidence score; needs_human triggers on the enumerated fact-conflict conditions only

spec.error_handling: Rule engine failure -> retry, then escalate to Data Correction queue; never defaults to pass.
spec.audit: Full rule trace (which rule fired, which fields it read) logged per claim.

spec.goal: Route claims with unresolved intake data problems to the Data Correction queue before coverage analysis, so agent steps never run against known-bad data.
spec.decision_logic: Deterministic routing condition on BR-01's own output field, not a re-evaluation.

spec.goal: Resolve a data-quality problem (missing fact, contradictory documents, identity mismatch) that blocks the claim from proceeding — explicitly distinct from a judgment-call escalation.
spec.trigger: GW-01 'yes' branch, or BR-00 identity mismatch.
spec.decision_logic: Reviewer requests/enters the missing fact or confirms identity manually; not a coverage judgment call.

grounding.reason: data-quality/identity correction, not a policy-coverage interpretation — nothing here is grounded in a PDS clause

escalation_target.distinct_from: HUM-02 Action Center (judgment calls) — kept as a separate queue/SLA per §10's escalation-queue-ownership pitfall, so a backlog metric on one doesn't mask the other

spec.audit: Reviewer identity, action taken, updated fields all logged.

spec.goal: Determine which policy cover(s) apply to the described incident, or that none apply.

inputs.context_source: PDS sections defining each cover type only (accidental damage, third party property damage, windscreen/window glass) — not the full PDS

spec.decision_logic: May finalize primary_recommendation autonomously only when exactly one cover has high confidence and no competing candidate is within the defined margin. May not invent a cover not present in the policy schedule.

grounding.fabrication_check: cited clause_id/quote exists verbatim in retrieved cover-definition sections
grounding.misapplication_check: cited clause actually defines the specific cover_type claimed, restricted to cover-definition clauses only — may not cite an exclusion clause to justify a cover classification

confidence_escalation_trigger.condition: confidence below threshold_set_id value, OR top two candidates within margin, OR a candidate's applicability depends on discretionary wording, OR a required fact is missing
confidence_escalation_trigger.calibration_dataset_version: none yet — not calibrated against labeled historical claims
confidence_escalation_trigger.calibration_owner: unassigned — must be named before this node is enabled for auto-processing

tools.name: policyholder_schedule_lookup
tools.when: always, to check which covers are held

guardrails: may not recommend a cover not on the policyholder's schedule
spec.error_handling: Schema-validation failure on output -> retry with correction prompt up to 3x, then escalate to Cover Classification Review — never guesses.
spec.audit: Full input narrative, retrieved context, model+prompt version, citation-verification result, and output logged per claim.

spec.goal: Determine whether any exclusion or carve-out defeats the cover(s) AG-02A identified.

inputs.context_source: exclusion/exception clauses relevant to the identified cover(s) only

spec.decision_logic: Evaluates only exclusions relevant to the already-classified cover(s). May identify a probable exclusion; may not issue a final adverse decision alone.

grounding.fabrication_check: cited exclusion clause exists verbatim in the retrieved set
grounding.misapplication_check: cited clause's actual exclusion scope covers the specific fact pattern claimed — restricted to exclusion/exception clauses only, may not cite a cover-definition clause

confidence_escalation_trigger.condition: discretionary wording present (e.g. 'reasonable', 'as soon as reasonably possible') OR contradictory evidence OR exclusion outcome differs materially across ambiguous cover candidates from AG-02A OR missing material fact OR low confidence

tools.name: pds_section_retriever
tools.when: always, scoped to exclusion/exception clauses for the classified cover(s)

guardrails: may not cite cover-definition clauses to justify an exclusion
may not issue a final adverse decision — flags only, GW-02 + HUM-02 own the actual adverse determination
spec.error_handling: Schema-validation failure -> retry x3 then escalate, never guesses.
spec.audit: Full input, retrieved context, model+prompt version, citation-verification result logged.

nodes.title: Outcome gateway, scoped by cause (coverage stage)

spec.goal: Route the coverage-stage outcome by CAUSE of adversity — never merge deterministic declines and agent-judgment adverse outcomes into the same branch.
spec.trigger: AG-02B 'excluded or needs_human' branch, or BR-01 fail.
spec.decision_logic: Deterministic routing rule, per §2's escalation scoping rule: (a) deterministic decline (lapsed/outside period/unpaid premium, from BR-01) -> auto-process -> async sampled QA lane, never a human hop. (b) agent-judgment adverse (AG-02B exclusion applied, discretionary clause, unresolved cover ambiguity, above delegated authority) -> HUM-02. (c) not excluded -> continue to BR-02.

grounding.reason: routing on upstream nodes' own typed outputs, not a new interpretation

spec.goal: Provide governance evidence that the population of auto-processed decisions (approved AND declined) is periodically checked, without sitting synchronously in the customer-facing critical path.
spec.trigger: Any auto-process branch (GW-02 or GW-03 'auto-process' edges), on a stratified sample — by risk tier, severity, model/prompt-version drift, or random percentage — run post-hoc against already-closed cases.
spec.decision_logic: Sampling policy is configuration, not per-claim judgment. NOT a mandatory gate: throughput of the mainline flow is unaffected.

grounding.reason: governance/sampling operation, not a coverage decision — a sampled review may itself re-check an underlying agent node's grounding, but this node's own logic cites nothing

escalation_target.circuit_breaker: if sampled error rate on a given node exceeds a configured threshold in a rolling window, that node is automatically forced back into synchronous human review (GW-02/GW-03 routing rules updated) until recalibrated — a dashboard-only report without this trigger is explicitly insufficient per §6

spec.audit: Sampled case, reviewer finding, and (if triggered) circuit-breaker state change all logged.
downstream_edges: finding: node error rate over threshold -> trip circuit breaker on that node

spec.goal: Resolve genuine ambiguity, contradiction, or discretion the source document leaves open, or approve/override an agent-judgment adverse outcome.
spec.trigger: Any agent-derived adverse or above-authority outcome (GW-02 or GW-03 'agent-judgment adverse' edge) — never a pure deterministic decline.

inputs.schema: {claim_packet, all prior agent outputs with citations, relevant issue-log entry if one exists, highlighted contradictions}

spec.decision_logic: Reviewer selects from the enumerated outcome set only — not free text as the sole record.

escalation_target.process_app: operational triage dashboard, distinct from a single Action Center task

grounding.reason: human decision, not an automated fabrication/misapplication check — but see citation_confirmation_requirement below, which is this node's equivalent discipline

spec.citation_confirmation_requirement: reviewer must confirm or select the controlling citation(s) before completion — the decision trail stays as auditable as the agent's
spec.audit: Reviewer identity, decision, override_notes, and confirmed citations all logged.
downstream_edges: approve -> BR-02 or SVC-03 (depending on which gateway routed here)
escalate_to_specialist -> (out of scope for this workflow — specialist queue)

nodes.title: Sub-limits, excess & waiting-period check
nodes.source_task_title: Check the specific cover's own conditions

spec.goal: Calculate the applicable excess (including waiver conditions) and confirm the claim is within any cover-specific sub-limit.
spec.trigger: AG-02B 'clean' branch, or HUM-02 'approve' where applicable.

inputs.schema: {cover_type, claim_facts (at-fault details supplied?, windscreen-only damage?), certificate_of_insurance excess schedule}

outputs.schema: {excess_payable: number, excess_waived: bool, sub_limit_applies: bool, sub_limit_amount: number|null, citation_refs[]}

spec.decision_logic: Hard rule table: standard excess waived only if not-at-fault AND at-fault driver name/address AND at-fault vehicle registration all supplied (not_at_fault_excess_waiver) — missing any one of the three means excess is payable. Windscreen-only damage claims are excess-free up to one claim per period (windscreen_cover), and a safely-repairable chip doesn't consume that one claim (windscreen_chip_repair). No discretion.

grounding.fabrication_check: every rule maps to a real clause
grounding.misapplication_check: not applicable — pre-verified rule table, same as BR-01

spec.error_handling: Rule engine failure -> retry, then route to HUM-02 rather than guessing an excess amount.

nodes.title: Draft settlement recommendation
nodes.source_task_title: Determine settlement path: repair or total loss

spec.goal: Produce a recommended settlement outcome, amount band, and rationale (decide only — see AG-04 for the separate customer-facing draft).

inputs.schema: {cover_classification, exclusion_analysis, policy_limits, excess_result, valuation_inputs, any human clarifications recorded upstream}

spec.decision_logic: May draft a recommendation within delegated $/risk-tier authority. May not issue a final adverse or above-authority decision without human sign-off. Repair-vs-total-loss determination follows total_loss's uneconomical-or-unsafe-to-repair test and State/Territory write-off criteria; stolen-car timing follows the 14-day rule (stolen_car_total_loss_timing).

grounding.misapplication_check: cited clause supports the specific coverage/payment-rationale statement made — checked on every coverage and payment-rationale statement, not just the headline outcome

confidence_escalation_trigger.condition: outcome is adverse or partial-adverse BECAUSE OF agent judgment (not a prior deterministic decline — GW-02/GW-03 already separated that) OR above delegated authority OR low confidence OR unresolved factual conflict OR any clause using discretionary language ('may', 'at its discretion')

tools.name: market_value_lookup
tools.when: when a total-loss valuation is required

guardrails: may not finalize an adverse outcome unsupervised
spec.error_handling: Schema-validation failure -> retry x3 then escalate.
spec.audit: Full input, retrieved context, model+prompt version, citation-verification result logged.

spec.goal: Produce customer-facing wording explaining the settlement outcome and rationale, in plain language, citing what was covered/excluded and why — deliberately a SEPARATE node from AG-03 (decide/draft split, per §5's explicit callout: a node that both decides and drafts customer wording should always be split).
spec.trigger: AG-03 'within authority & clean' branch, or HUM-02 approve on a settlement decision.

inputs.schema: {ag_03.recommended_outcome, ag_03.rationale, ag_03.citation_refs, customer communication style guide}

spec.decision_logic: Rewords AG-03's already-decided outcome for a customer audience. Does not re-decide the outcome — no new coverage judgment happens in this node.

grounding.fabrication_check: every clause referenced in the customer letter exists verbatim in AG-03's already-verified citation_refs (no new citations introduced)
grounding.misapplication_check: wording doesn't overstate/understate what AG-03 actually decided

spec.error_handling: Schema-validation failure -> retry x3 then falls back to a template letter + flags for human wording review (never sends an unvalidated draft).

nodes.title: Outcome gateway, scoped by cause (settlement stage)

spec.goal: Same cause-scoped test as GW-02, applied to the settlement outcome — kept as a structurally separate gateway rather than reusing GW-02, since it evaluates a different upstream node's output.
spec.decision_logic: agent-judgment adverse / over-authority (from AG-03) -> HUM-02. clean / within authority -> auto-process -> QA-01.

grounding.reason: routing on AG-03's own typed output

nodes.title: Generate outcome letter & write back to claims system

spec.goal: Persist the final decision to the claims system and dispatch the outcome letter, then close the coverage-determination subprocess.
spec.trigger: GW-02 deterministic-decline branch, GW-03 clean branch, or HUM-02 override/approve.
spec.error_handling: Write-back failure -> retry with backoff, then alert ops (claim stays open, not silently lost).
spec.audit: Full write-back payload + dispatch confirmation logged; this is the terminal audit record for the coverage-determination subprocess.
downstream_edges: always -> close (Maestro Case: claim lifecycle continues outside this subprocess)
